pages.title: Retrieval practice and spaced repetition
paragraphs: Retrieval practice strengthens memory by recalling information without looking at notes. Active recall is different from rereading. Close the book, answer a question, then check the answer.
Spaced repetition distributes practice across several days. Review material after one day, three days, and seven days. The schedule is an example, not a universal rule.

pages.title: Cognitive load and study design
paragraphs: Working memory has limited capacity. A visual slide should focus on one central idea and show its source page. Short explanations help learners connect spoken examples with the lecture material.
Combine an active recall question with a spaced review plan. Use feedback to find errors, revise the explanation, and try again later.
